title: Extending Myerson's Optimal Auctions to Correlated Bidders via Neural Network Interpolation
claim: Start from a non-monotone optimal-greedy rule, smooth it into a verifiably monotone form, then repair revenue while keeping strategy-proofness.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, shared axes, colored allocation regions with letter labels
description: Four side-by-side square plots, each with both axes running 0 to 1, show allocation regions for a two-bidder auction. Red fills the upper-left region (bidder 2 wins) and blue fills the lower-right region (bidder 1 wins). Panel (a), monotone allocation, has a white no-sale region between them, labeled A (blue) and B (red). Panel (b), greedy allocation, has the same layout with a jagged boundary and a few small red and blue dots marking monotonicity violations. Panel (c), interpolation, has a smooth boundary with no white region, labeled B+D and A+C. Panel (d), revenue fix, restores a white-derived no-sale area as lighter pink (D) and lighter blue (C) bands, split by a dashed curve. Serif captions sit under each panel. The eye goes first to the large red and blue shapes.
caption: Illustration of a 2-bidder setting where axes represent two bids in $[0,1]$. Blue and red regions denote wins for bidder 1 and 2, respectively. (a) monotone allocation: A strategy-proof allocation where a winner necessarily remains the winner after a unilateral bid increase. (b) greedy allocation (based on marginal profits): Non-monotone allocation that gives the revenue upper bound --- red and blue points enclosed in opposing regions represent monotonicity violations that preclude strategy-proofness. (c) (monotone) interpolation: A tiny neural network mimics the macro-trends of (b) while "glossing over" fine-grained violations due to its limited expressive capacity. This interpolation is formally verified to be monotone, thereby ensuring exact strategy-proofness. (d) revenue fix (leading to final allocation): The result after applying the revenue fix in Section [ref], which determines the exact shape of the "no-sale" (white) region to maximize expected revenue without altering the strategy-proofness established in the previous stage.
abstract: We aim to design revenue-maximizing single-item auctions that are deterministic, strategy-proof, and ex post individually rational --- the quintessential fundamental model for optimal mechanism design. While Myerson's seminal work solved this model for independent bidders, straightforward extensions to correlated settings often result in non-monotonic, and therefore non-strategy-proof allocations. Critically, optimal allocation design for correlated bidders is NP-hard to approximate, rendering theoretical optimality guarantees in this domain computationally intractable. We establish a new standard of empirical rigor for this theoretically hard model by proposing an empirical pipeline. We synthesize neural interpolation of Myerson's greedy allocation based on marginal profits (the correlated variant of virtual valuation), formal neural verification to enforce exact strategy-proofness, and a constructive repair procedure. Empirically, our method is highly effective, consistently achieves near-optimal revenue across a wide range of distributions, including synthetic, adversarial, and real-world (consumer, financial, and industrial) datasets. Compared to existing manual and neural baselines, our approach shows substantial improvement, often reducing the revenue gap by an order of magnitude. Our study is also the first to introduce (unattainable) greedy revenue as a rigorous upper bound for empirical benchmarking, providing a definitive quantitative performance measure where true optima remain theoretically elusive. We demonstrate the generality of our approach by extending it to multi-unit auctions with unit demand and integrating our verification techniques into RegretNet to achieve exact strategy-proofness.
